headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and capability conflict: Goose’s filesystem/MCP/network defaults can ingest and act on content from a non-isolated prompt-listing agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing prompt repository with no runtime isolation, while profile B reads/writes the filesystem and uses MCP extensions. If A’s prompt content is placed in B’s workspace, B can treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The shared filesystem bridge makes injection plausible in default use, though not proven as a direct parser exploit.
conditions: IF profile A content is copied into a directory that profile B reads
IF profile B loads file contents or MCP payloads without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep A’s content in a read-only directory
Disable MCP extensions for untrusted content
Require a manual review step before B consumes any file from A
Use separate workspaces for A and B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files passed into B

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read files and has broad network egress, so any sensitive files in the shared workspace can be transmitted outward. A itself has no egress and appears to be a static prompt-listing source, so the leakage path is primarily from shared files into B’s outputs or network calls. The pair is not isolated by default, so the risk exists in common setups.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the workspace B can read
IF B is configured to send file contents to configured model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of B’s workspace
Restrict B’s network egress to approved endpoints
Run B in a separate user account or container
Audit which files B can read before starting
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable content, but B has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared filesystem state across instances. If A’s materials are stored in the same repo or directory, B can overwrite or race on mutable files and git state by default. Because B’s defaults include broad write access and no isolation, the conflict can cause irreversible repository changes.
conditions: IF A and B operate on the same working directory or git repository
IF multiple B instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Use separate repositories for A and B
Pause extra B instances before editing shared files
Commit or stash changes before starting B
Limit B to a throwaway branch
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces prompt content, and B can ingest files and act through shell, git, and MCP tools. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors or malicious instructions can cascade into edits or external actions. B does have user-confirmation hooks, so the pathway is not fully automatic, but verification is not guaranteed by default.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as task instructions or facts
IF B executes shell, git, or MCP actions based on that text without independent verification
mitigations: Require B to summarize and verify A’s output before acting
Disable automatic execution of A-derived instructions
Use a second reviewer for any shell or git action
Mark A outputs as untrusted in the workflow
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before actions

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public prompt repository with no touched data classes, while B handles source code and files in cwd. No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so a compliance issue is not established. The only plausible concern is general handling of workspace files by B, which is not enough for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s workspace
IF an external policy requires residency or retention controls not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Review retention settings before use
Separate code and regulated data repositories
Document the data class allowed for B
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets
